original_question_en: Which minimal graphs prevent Ramsey numbers from growing linearly with the number of edges? Characterize these obstructions.
definition_used: G is Ramsey size linear if there is c > 0 with r(G,H) <= c * e(H) for every graph H with no isolated vertices (Erdos-Faudree-Rousseau-Schelp 1993). A minimal Ramsey obstruction is a non-RSL graph all of whose proper subgraphs are RSL.
references: EFRS93 P. Erdos, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau, R. H. Schelp, Ramsey size linear graphs, Combin. Probab. Comput. 2 (1993) 389-399, doi:10.1017/s096354830000078x
Wi24 Y. Wigderson, Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size-linear graphs, arXiv:2409.05931 (2024)
notes: jsp_000096_main has two parts. Part 1 (the characterisation of the obstructions asked for by the catalog) is proved unconditionally. Part 2 (Wigderson's infinitude theorem) is proved on the two explicit analytic hypotheses of his proof: (a) acyclic graphs are Ramsey size linear, (b) graphs of arbitrarily large girth that are not Ramsey size linear. See ACCEPTANCE.md and discovery policy.json blockers for the exact missing lemmas.
